0.0.n: This is the name of Japan’s lower house of parliament.

0.1.n: が marks the House of Representatives as what undergoes dissolution.

0.2.n: 解散する becomes passive 解散される, then past 解散された, showing that dissolution has occurred.

0.3.n: とき follows a clause to identify the time or situation being discussed.

0.4.n: は marks the whole situation of dissolution as the topic of the question.

1.0.n: This noun refers to formally ending the current House of Representatives.

1.1.n: の links dissolution to its date; Japanese puts the describing noun first.

1.2.n: 日 refers to the calendar date on which dissolution occurs.

1.3.n: から marks the dissolution date as the starting point for counting days.

1.4.n: 何 asks for a number, and 日 counts days.

1.5.n: 以内 sets an upper limit and includes the stated number of days.

1.6.n: に marks the time limit within which the election must take place.

2.0.n: This names Japan’s lower house and combines with 選挙 to specify the election.

2.1.n: Together with 衆議院, this identifies an election for the lower house.

2.2.n: を marks the election as the thing that must be conducted.

2.3.n: 行う becomes 行わなければならない, literally if one does not conduct it, that will not do, expressing obligation.

2.4.n: か ends the sentence as a direct question about the required time limit.

3.0.n: This noun stands alone to introduce the response to the question.

4.0.n: 日 attaches to the number 40 to count a duration in days.

4.1.n: 以内 includes the fortieth day as the latest permitted day.

0.lit: As for when the House of Representatives has been dissolved,
0.tip: The past form before とき shows dissolution is complete before the election takes place.

1.lit: From the day of dissolution, within how many days,
1.tip: から marks the starting point, while 以内に sets the deadline.

2.lit: Must one hold a House of Representatives election?
2.tip: なければならない expresses must, even though its parts are negative.

3.tip: Japanese can introduce an answer with just the noun 答え, without a full sentence.

4.tip: 以内 includes the stated limit, so day 40 is still within the deadline.
